intended_use: browser visualizer for evaluating stacked alpha-masked cloud planes
units: scene units; starting dimensions mirror the C4D demo approximately
assumptions: The browser artifact is a visual approximation, not a physically simulated volume.
The C4D Alpha Noise setup is represented with GLSL procedural noise rather than a byte-for-byte C4D shader clone.
All layers share one evolving 3D field and one time source so the cloud develops coherently.
Lower rounding layers are signed negative-height slices that contract in footprint and opacity toward the bottom.
Lighting is a density-aware shader approximation with one movable point source, not physical multiple scattering.
validation: Controls update the visible cloud without page reload.
Layer count and spacing alter the stack geometry.
Noise type, octaves, clips, and clip ramp alter the alpha field.
Animation can be paused and resumed; reduced-motion preference is respected for initial playback.
Current settings and camera state can be exported as versioned JSON and imported again with bounded validation.
Light azimuth, elevation, distance, intensity, ambient fill, color, visibility, and orbit state are saved with the settings.
Moving the light above, beside, and below the cloud changes diffuse shading, density self-shadowing, and edge scattering.
Lower rounding layers visibly contract beneath the main stack without exceeding the 64-instance budget.
The visualizer remains usable at narrow browser widths.
